headline: Motion, ripple, reduced motion and the six looks work as D140 says, and the lived-in journeys, route sweep and 13 breakage checks are green; but `pnpm typecheck` fails on the branch, sheets never ease to a new height (the hook never attaches), Home from a pushed screen slides back instead of crossfading, and nothing tests the web app's call into the shell's haptic (two probes survived). I had no Agent tool: I ran the sweep and the eyes pass myself.

findings.title: `pnpm typecheck` fails on the branch, so CI is red
findings.detail: `apps/web/src/lib/haptics.ts` line 38: the two `return`s inside `.then((v) => {...})` have different promise types (`Promise<{performed:boolean}|undefined>` and `Promise<void|undefined>`). Vite doesn't typecheck, so the app builds and the e2e passes; the brief's Done-when says the code checks are clean.

findings.title: Sheets never ease to a new height: `useSheetResize` never attaches
findings.detail: The hook runs in `Sheet` on `[area, open]`, but the sheet's content is mounted by Radix's portal after the effect runs, so `area.current` is null and it returns without observing. No `ResizeObserver` is ever attached to a sheet's scroll area and `Element.animate` is never called. The category sheet going from its list (732 px) to *From now on / Just this one* (285 px) jumps; frames sampled every rAF for 500 ms saw only 732 and 285. Brief §3 and patterns §8 (*A sheet whose content changes eases to its new height*) are not met, and no test covers it.
findings.repro: qa/e2e/b05feel-sheet.spec.ts (FLOW-9b) and b05feel-sheet2.spec.ts, against a preview build: open a payment, tap its category, pick a category

findings.title: The Home tab, tapped from a pushed screen, slides back instead of crossfading
findings.detail: `TabBar.toHome` goes back through history (`history.go(homeIndex - here)`) when Home is behind, so the router sees a screen-to-tab pop and plays `back` (the pushed screen slides out right). patterns §8: *A tab switch crossfades, a tab tapped from a pushed screen too*. The Review tab from a pushed screen does crossfade. The repo's own motion.spec misses it because it opens the pushed screen as history index 0, so `homeIndex` is unset and it takes the replace path. `motion.test.ts` pins `screenChange` only, not this path.
findings.repro: Home, More, Payments, then the Home tab; recorded `document.startViewTransition` types (qa/e2e/b05feel-motion.spec.ts FLOW-2)

findings.title: Nothing tests the web app calling the shell's `haptic`; two probes on it survived
findings.detail: The brief wants haptics proved by an emulator test of the bridge call. `ShellTest` calls the native method, but the web side (`lib/haptics.ts`: check `info().bridge >= 2`, call `SenShell.haptic`, swallow a failure, v1 gets none) has no test: motion.spec's haptics test reads `__senHaptics`, which `haptic()` fills *before* it looks at the shell. Removing the bridge call, or calling it on a bridge-1 shell, leaves every suite green. With a stub shell (FLOW-8) the behaviour is right today: v1 makes 0 calls, v2 makes `toggle-on`/`toggle-off`, a throwing shell is swallowed.  The `FieldError` reject haptic has no test either (its focus guard survived).
findings.repro: Probe in a worktree: delete `if (v >= 2) return SenShell.haptic({ kind: NATIVE[kind] }).catch(() => undefined);`, then `pnpm exec vitest run` and `playwright test motion.spec`

findings.title: Every tap now has a DOM-mutation tail, so 17 of the 21 metrics flags are the ripple, and `step.settleMs` can no longer see real settling under about 430 ms
findings.detail: `step.settleMs` is the last DOM mutation after the tap. The ripple adds `data-up` about 120 ms after the press and removes its node about 425-440 ms after it, on every tap that stays on its screen. Measured with a MutationObserver on a bare tap: mutations at 22 ms, 141 ms (`press`), 442 ms (`tab on active`) with motion, 425 ms with reduced motion. That matches the flagged steps (422-684 ms against main's 59-248; the ones that navigate show about 120-135 ms because the host is removed). `money-in/2` (+643) and `proposal/3` (+759) are that tail plus a 200-400 ms view transition (inferred from the sum, not separately measured). Recommendation: the metric should ignore `.press` mutations (`apps/web/e2e/metrics.ts`).

findings.title: Taps are blocked for 400-1280 ms by a tab transition at 4x CPU; patterns says none is longer than 200 ms
findings.detail: patterns §8 *Speed*: taps are blocked while a screen transition runs, so none is longer than 200 ms. At the metrics' CPU 4x, a tab switch's view transition took 403-509 ms in total (150-200 ms before it even started), and 1277 ms (912 ms to start) for a second visit to Insights. Push: the new screen reaches the DOM 128-199 ms after the tap against 66-137 ms with motion reduced. The metrics' `step.firstChangeMs` doesn't flag it because the ripple answers in the first frame; no flag exists for the screen arriving late. The handoff already names the lever (tabs switch at once). The remaining `step:ask/3` flag (2401 ms against 137 on main) is, I think, this plus the Insights screen's own 2.2-2.7 s settle, but I did not prove that.

findings.title: With motion on and a slow CPU, journeys fail that pass on main (2 of 76 head journey runs, 0 of 76 on main)
findings.detail: `metrics-head` failed `subscription` (strict-mode: `getByText('Claude Pro')` matched three elements of the old Insights screen, so the old screen was still in the DOM after the tap returned and `settled` passed) and `film-head` failed `scan-after` (`Reading receipt…` never seen in 20 s). Both fit the new screen's commit being held by the view transition's capture; I reproduced neither in isolation (scan-after passes at 4x CPU with motion on, 11 polls saw the text). The functional suite is safe because it runs reduced; the feel pass is not. `confirm-steps-head` ran 34 journeys with 0 failures.

findings.title: Small gaps: no ripple on `<summary>` rows; a failed `info()` turns haptics off for the session; `reject` skips an Enter-submitted form
findings.detail: (a) `TAPPABLE` in `frame/press.ts` has no `summary`, so the two disclosure rows (`settings/email.tsx:65`, `capture/apps.tsx:86`) get no ripple. (b) `bridgeVersion()` caches `0` when `SenShell.info()` rejects once, so haptics stay off until the app restarts. (c) `FieldError` skips the reject haptic when focus is in an input, so an error shown after Enter in a field is silent; tapping a button is felt. Read from code; (a) is also seen in the DOM (12 of 12 tappables on Home had ripples, summaries are not on Home).

findings.title: Metrics flags other than the ripple: both re-measured, neither is a standing cost
findings.detail: `screen:insights/year` settle 2184 ms (main 1258): re-measured 5 times a side: head [2106,1303,2067,1347,1495], main [1553,2449,1999,1138,2258]; blocking is the same. `screen:new-look` blocking 703 ms (main 0): re-measured 5 times: head [0,0,568,0,0], main [0,0,0,0,0]. One in five spikes on the branch; I could not find the cause (the screen runs its own view transition, and in isolation under 4x CPU both builds show 240-270 ms of long tasks). Accepted as intermittent; worth a look if it recurs.

findings.title: How this run differed from the skill
findings.detail: The reviewer had no Agent tool, so the sweep was run by me from a script (not a Haiku helper) and the eyes pass was done by me (Sonnet), not `qa-eyes`. The sweep ran `pnpm test:db` and `e2e:server` before Postgres was up (both failed in 1 s and 13 s); I started it and re-ran both: they pass. The qa-diff catalogue shows 3 entries with pixel changes of at most 1/255 (anti-aliasing), so the catalogued screens are unchanged, as the brief says. A unit test (`fake.test.ts` year) timed out once under heavy CPU load during a probe run.
